title: Contract risk to pricing heuristics and SSQ clause linkage matrix
creator: Priya Nambiar
description:
Problem: Enterprise sales cycles are prolonged when legal redlines around liability, indemnity, and data handling create ad-hoc pricing concessions. We lack a standard, auditable correlation between contract risk deviations and list-price adjustments. SSQ (security questionnaire) answers are often used qualitatively in negotiations but not programmatically tied to recommended concession bands.

Proposal: Create a standardized "Contract Risk → Pricing" heuristic matrix that maps common MSA/DPA redline buckets to discrete pricing adjustment recommendations (percent discount, credit escrow, or security engineering remediation commitments). Link each redline bucket to the SSQ evidence/coverage that typically mitigates that risk (e.g., encryption-at-rest + KMS = reduce liability cap concession by X%). Deliverables: a canonical clause taxonomy, the mapping matrix (CSV + Confluence doc), sales-facing guidance document, and a plan for integrating recommended adjustments into quoting tooling (later phase).

Scope: Enterprise MSA/DPA redlines for mid-market and enterprise segments only. Focus on 12 high-frequency clauses (~indemnity, liability cap tiers, escrow, breach notification, subprocessor controls, data residency, audit rights, retention). Exclusions: bespoke carrier or insurance negotiation, and negotiated partner reseller agreements.

Metrics for success: Reduce average contract negotiation duration for targeted deals from 27 days to <=19 days (30% improvement) and increase close rate on negotiated deals by 10-15% within 3 months of rollout. Track # of legal exceptions auto-classified and % of pricing recommendations accepted by sales.

Owners & stakeholders: PM (Priya Nambiar) owning product definition; Sales Ops (Lena Ortiz) owning pilot with AMs; Legal (Avery Cole) owning clause taxonomy; Security (Dr. Ethan Wells) owning SSQ evidence mapping; Engineering (Marco Ruiz) owning later integration feed.

Risks and trade-offs: - Hard boundaries across risk tiers can lead to edge-case disputes; include an explicit escalation path to Legal for overrides. - Pricing recommendations must be conservative at first to avoid revenue leakage; build telemetry to iterate. - Security evidence maturity varies by customer size; allow manual override and evidence submission path.

High-level timeline: Week 0-2: research & clause frequency analysis; Week 2-4: draft matrix + Sales playbook; Week 5-6: pilot with 6 AMs; Week 7: review pilot telemetry and Legal sign-off; Week 8: iterate and prepare integration backlog.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical clause taxonomy for top 12 redline buckets published to Confluence
Mapping matrix (CSV) that links each redline bucket to 1) risk tier (low/medium/high), 2) recommended pricing adjustment band, and 3) SSQ evidence types that reduce risk
Sales-facing guidance doc with 3 negotiation scripts and example concessions per tier
Pilot set up with 6 AMs and tracked using Deal Desk spreadsheet + simple dashboard
Legal has reviewed and signed off on escalation criteria and override workflow
